item.title: Book Club: Animal Life — Icelandic Canadian Club of Toronto
item.description:
Session Four: DEC 15, 2026 Animal Life, Auður Ava Ólafsdóttir, 2022 Fiction During a snowy Christmas season in Reykjavík, a lonely middle-aged woman unexpectedly becomes connected to a young pregnant immigrant and her child. A tender and often humorous novel about family, belonging, aging, and human connection.

\n

item.title: Book Club: In Valhalla’s Shadows — Icelandic Canadian Club of Toronto
item.description:
Session Three: NOV 17, 2026 In Valhalla’s Shadows, W.D. Valgardson, 2019 Mystery/Noir Set in Manitoba’s Icelandic community, this atmospheric mystery follows a retired police officer investigating a decades-old disappearance. Valgardson combines Nordic noir elements with prairie history, memory, family secrets, and questions of identity.

item.title: Book Club for November 2026 — Icelandic Roots
item.description: by Gayle Graham It is a pleasure to invite you to the November 5th Icelandic Roots Book Club to hear from Cathie Eliasson, the author of Falcons Forever: the Saga of the 1920 Olympic Gold Medal Ice Hockey Team. The book chronicles the Winnipeg Falcons' journey to the VII Olympiad in Antwerp, Belgium, where they won the very first gold medal in men's ice hockey. This group of first-generation Western Icelandic Canadians had just returned from fighting in World War I and had to overcome...

item.title: Rok — Icelandic Roots
item.description: By Gunnar Birgisson The weather plays an oversized role in Icelandic life, much more so than in most other places. And when it comes to weather, the wind is a major player. In Iceland, the wind is such a constant element of life that people can be surprised when there’s a day without notable wind. The complete absence of wind, logn, can leave people baffled, as if their long-time nemesis had unexpectedly retreated, probably to prepare for a more vicious attack. Rok is just one type of...
